subject: Hummingbird: persistent long-tail completions — exec readout requested
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hummingbird.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: anita.verma@hummingbird.ai; support@hummingbird.ai
Date: 2029-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production tail latency — urgent

Evelyn,

We started seeing a spike in p99/p999 completion times across multiple routes this morning around 02:40 UTC. Symptoms: long-tail completions (several requests >6s), intermittent 500s for large prompts, and a surge in queued requests for our busiest endpoint. This is impacting our user experience for multi-turn flows.

We attached a csv of representative requests and a short trace pdf. Could Redwood run a short triage and let us know whether this looks like a capacity congestion / backpressure issue or something else (model/kernel/regression)? We can prioritize a call if needed.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
VP Engineering
Hummingbird AI

Attachments: hummingbird-p99-traces-20291004.pdf, hb-request-samples.csv

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hummingbird.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-10-04T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production tail latency — urgent

Sanjay — thanks for the heads-up and for the traces. We’re starting a focused triage now. Initial ask: can you confirm the primary model and the typical max sequence length for the failing requests? Also, are you pinned to a model variant in your workspace or using hosted defaults?

Quick context for your team: we’ll look at queueing/backpressure signals (request queue depth, worker saturation), concurrency caps at the per-customer layer, and KV cache hit rates. If needed we can route traffic to a lower-cost, high-concurrency variant temporarily to drain queues while we fix the root cause.

I’ll loop in Aditya for runtime-level traces and Grace for account routing/fallbacks. I’ll follow up with an exec readout if we see customer-impacting SLAs.

—Evelyn Hart
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-proposal-v2.md (draft runbook for queue/backpressure drills)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, sanjay@hummingbird.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-10-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production tail latency — urgent

Quick notes from runtime traces (preliminary):
- We see repeated request batching delays on the cluster serving Hummingbird; average batching wait up 40–120ms, but the outliers correspond to windows where worker pods are saturated and token generation stalls.
- Concurrency caps are being hit on several routes: customer-level concurrency set to 120 concurrent streams; observed instantaneous requests >150, causing queuing at the proxy layer.
- Backpressure propagated: several long-running completions held KV locks leading to slower cache warmups and additional stall amplification.
- No kernel regression detected in the last deploy window based on hash/variant checks; however, we saw a transient increase in model memory pressure consistent with token-length spikes.

Immediate actions underway:
1) bump temporary concurrency cap to 200 for HB routes (will require exec approval if maintained >48h).
2) enable aggressive prefix caching for high-frequency prefixes in the short-term.
3) apply an emergency routing policy to route low-latency traffic to the lower-latency quantized variant (compatible fallback).

I’m collecting traces into INF-4321. Expect a 30–45m update with data-backed recommendations.

—Aditya Rao
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, sanjay@hummingbird.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-10-04T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production tail latency — urgent

Evelyn / team — operational note: I initiated the temp routing policy at 11:15 UTC and saw queue depth drop ~65% in ten minutes for the affected route. Observed error spikes (500s) dropped to baseline. However, we did notice a small increase in token cost per request for the fallback path (quantized variant has slightly lower throughput for very long sequences).

Metrics summary (11:00–11:30 UTC):
- p95: 320ms -> 280ms
- p99: 2.2s -> 820ms post-routing change
- queued requests: 1.8k -> 600
- 500 errors: 43 -> 7

Next steps proposed:
- Keep routing policy for 2–4 hours while we drain long requests.
- If sustained, propose a one-week concurrency cap increase for HB to 160 while engineering works on request shaping and KV cache improvements. That requires sign-off from sales ops/finance for potential unit-cost delta.
- Prepare a short exec readout (15m) for 16:00 PT today to align on credit/crediting request and escalation path.

Laura Bennett
Director, Incident Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: hummingbird-p99-traces-20291004.pdf

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hummingbird.ai>, Anita Verma <anita.verma@hummingbird.ai>
Date: 2029-10-04T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production tail latency — urgent (Exec readout scheduled)

Team — summary + ask for execs: we reduced immediate customer impact via an emergency routing policy and saw substantial improvements. Root-cause appears to be a confluence of: sustained request bursts above configured concurrency caps, long-sequence KV lock contention, and a small window of model memory pressure that amplified batching delays.

Action items before the 16:00 PT exec readout:
- Aditya: finalize a short tech memo (1-pager) on the KV contention pattern and a recommended engineering fix (due 15:00 PT).
- Laura: confirm estimated incremental unit cost delta for a temporary cap increase to 160 and a two-day extended routing policy (due 15:30 PT).
- Grace: prepare two options for the customer: (A) 1-week temporary cap increase + proactive rate-shaping with an estimated credit, (B) keep current cap + invest in a 6-week engineering fix roadmap — include expected SLA impact for both.

Sanjay / Anita — we will present the technical findings and proposed options at 16:00 PT. We appreciate the quick traces you provided; that helped narrow the investigation.

If execs approve, we’ll also propose a small customer credit to offset the cost delta and commit to a runbook change so this doesn’t re-occur.

—Evelyn Hart
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
